A $10\text{ cm}$ diameter jet of water strikes a curved vane with a velocity of $25\text{ m/s}$. The inlet angle of the vane is zero and the outlet angle is $150^\circ$ measured with respect to the impinging jet direction. Determine the resultant force on the vane when the vane is stationary.

questions.text: An inward-flow reaction turbine has an inlet guide vane angle of $30^\circ$ and inward edges of the runner blade at $115^\circ$ to the direction of rotation. The breadth of the runner at the inlet is a quarter of the inlet diameter and there is no whirl velocity at the outlet. The gross head is $20\text{ m}$ and the speed is $1000\text{ r.p.m.}$ The hydraulic and overall efficiencies may be assumed to be $88\%$ and $85\%$ respectively. Estimate the runner diameter at inlet and the power developed.

sub_questions.text: What are the different characteristics of Francis turbine? Discuss any one of them.

A Francis turbine develops $800\text{ kW}$ at an efficiency of $90\%$ under a net head of $12\text{ m}$. The draft tube used in this setup is a vertical cylindrical pipe of $2\text{ m}$ diameter. (a) What increase in power could be expected if a tapering vertical draft tube having an outlet diameter of $2.5\text{ m}$ replaces the existing cylindrical draft tube? (b) What would be the increase in the overall efficiency? Assume that the head, speed and discharge remain the same and there are no additional friction losses due to the new draft tube.
Explain different component parts of a centrifugal pump.

A centrifugal pump delivers water at the rate of $40\text{ litres/sec}$ for a total head of $30\text{ m}$. Find the output of the pump. If the overall efficiency of the set consisting of the pump and the electric motor is $75\%$, find the power required to drive the motor.

questions.text: A centrifugal pump is required to discharge $600\text{ litres/sec}$ of water and develop a head of $15\text{ m}$ when the impeller rotates at $750\text{ r.p.m.}$ The manometric efficiency is $0.80$. The loss of head in the pump due to fluid resistance can be assumed to be $0.027V^2$ where, $V =$ velocity with which the water leaves the impeller. Water enters the impeller without shock and whirl and the velocity of flow is $3.2\text{ m/s}$. Determine the (a) impeller diameter, (b) blade angle at outlet and (c) outlet area.

sub_questions.text: Define slip in a reciprocating pump. Explain the phenomenon of negative slip.

A single-acting reciprocating pump has a plunger of diameter of $250\text{ mm}$ and stroke of $350\text{ mm}$. If the speed of the pump is $60\text{ r.p.m.}$ and if it delivers $16.5\text{ litres/sec}$ of water against a suction head of $5\text{ m}$ and a delivery head of $20\text{ m}$, find the theoretical discharge, coefficient of discharge, slip, the percentage slip of the pump and the power required to drive the pump.
